title: Brothers and sisters, look at this image.
paragraphs:
Brothers and sisters, look at this image.
Many pastors post this and say, “This is how ministry feels.”
They’re pierced with betrayal, stress, criticism, and disappointment — and yes, ministry can truly be heavy.

But listen carefully, Gospel Warriors:
It was never meant to destroy you.
It only becomes unbearable when John 3:30 is not followed.
“He must increase, but I must decrease.” – John 3:30

💔 WHY MANY PASTORS FEEL LIKE THIS:
Because many start in the Spirit but end up carrying the burden in the flesh.
They begin for Christ but start building for themselves.
The pain multiplies when self increases — because the more “I” grows, the heavier ministry becomes.
Let’s break this down:

⚔️ 1️⃣ Financial Crisis → “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
When self increases, we worry about provision, approval, and numbers.
But when Christ increases, we rest in His supply.
He feeds His servants as He fed Elijah with ravens.
When it’s about Him, the source is Heaven — not people.

⚔️ 2️⃣ Issues and Betrayal → “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
When self is still alive, betrayal cuts deep.
But when Christ lives in us, we understand — it’s not rejection, it’s redirection.
Jesus was betrayed too, yet He never became bitter.
He said, “Father, forgive them.” That’s the strength of someone fully surrendered.

⚔️ 3️⃣ Stress and Disappointment → “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
Stress comes when we try to control what only God can handle.
Disappointment comes when we expect from people what only Christ can give.
But when we decrease, peace increases.
We let go of results and trust in the fruit God alone can produce.

⚔️ 4️⃣ Criticism and Family Pressure → “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
When we live for people’s approval, their criticism breaks us.
When we live for God’s glory, their criticism shapes us.
Even family may not understand your calling, but the One who called you will sustain you.

⚔️ 5️⃣ Persecution → “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
If we focus on self, persecution feels like an attack.
But if we focus on Christ, persecution becomes confirmation — that we are walking the narrow path.
The early apostles rejoiced when they were persecuted because they were counted worthy to suffer for His name.
🔥 WHY JOHN 3:30 IS NON-NEGOTIABLE FOR GOSPEL WARRIORS:

Because it’s the key to survival in battle.
When “I” decreases:
Pride dies.
Fear fades.
Stress breaks.
Offense loses grip.
Burnout becomes breakthrough.

Every arrow that hits self, stops when self is gone.
You can’t wound a dead man — and true discipleship means dying daily so that Christ may live fully.

💥 That’s why for us, the Gospel Warriors, John 3:30 is not just a verse — it’s our code of war.
It’s how we conquer ourselves before we conquer the world.

🕊 FINAL CHARGE:
Bro and sis, the goal is not to survive ministry — it’s to surrender in ministry.
Because when He increases and you decrease, no arrow can destroy you.
They may hit your body, but they will never pierce your spirit.
⚔️ Let this be our declaration today:

“Lord, less of me, more of You.
Empty me of pride, fill me with power.
Take away my name, that only Yours be remembered.”
